| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.13260-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13260) | **Beyond the Fast Rotators: A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury Survey of Substellar Weather**  |
|| N. Oliveros-Gomez, et al. -- incl., <mark>B. C. Estrada</mark>, <mark>A. v. Stauffenberg</mark> |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-12*|
|*Comments*| *White paper submitted to the "Multi-Cycle Treasury Program Concepts with JWST" call, Nov 2026*|
|**Abstract**|            Atmospheric variability provides a unique window into the three-dimensional structure, dynamics, and evolution of brown dwarf and giant exoplanet atmospheres. Recent JWST time-resolved spectroscopic observations have revealed complex wavelength-dependent variability, offering unprecedented insights into cloud structures, thermal perturbations, and atmospheric chemistry. However, existing programs have focused primarily on individual benchmarks and specific scientific questions, resulting in heterogeneous spectral and temporal coverage and leaving important regions of the substellar population underexplored, particularly across a broad range of rotation periods, spectral types, and viewing geometries. A JWST Multi-Cycle Treasury program could systematically investigate substellar weather across a diverse, well-characterized population. By combining broad infrared spectroscopic coverage with observations spanning multiple rotations and strategically selected epochs, this program would constrain the contributions of different physical mechanisms while investigating how atmospheric structures depend on rotation, viewing geometry, and fundamental physical properties. Extended monitoring would also improve rotational-period determinations and reveal how atmospheric features evolve from rotation to rotation and over longer timescales. This coordinated effort would provide a consistently designed and uniformly processed dataset of time-resolved spectra and variability diagnostics, enabling population-level comparisons, testing predictions from three-dimensional circulation models, and establishing a framework for interpreting the atmospheric diversity and evolution of brown dwarfs and directly imaged giant exoplanets.         |

| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.13343-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13343) | **A TESS Disappearing Act: The Vanishing Transits of TOI-2535 b**  |
|| S. W. Yee, et al. -- incl., <mark>T. Henning</mark> |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-12*|
|*Comments*| *5 figures, 17 pages + appendices. Published in ApJ Letters. Animated schematic for one possible system architecture available at this https URL*|
|**Abstract**|            Planetary transits require a fortuitous alignment between a planet's orbit and our line of sight, but dynamical interactions can render this geometric coincidence only temporary. We report the discovery of the hot Jupiter TOI-2535 b, the first confirmed planet orbiting a single star whose transits have been directly observed to disappear. Over seven years of photometry from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), the planet's transit chord traversed and eventually moved off the stellar disk entirely, with an impact parameter changing at the rate of $\dot{b} = 0.16\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. The transit mid-times also show significant departures of $\pm 6$ hours from a linear ephemeris. Joint modeling of the transit timing and duration variations (TTVs and TDVs) and NEID radial-velocity data indicates the presence of a nearby, mutually inclined ($i_\mathrm{mut} \gtrsim 5^\circ$) planetary perturber, with the TDV being primarily due to precession of the planets' orbital planes. Our dynamical modeling reveals that the perturber is likely of Saturn-mass or greater and in a mean-motion resonance with TOI-2535 b, making this an unusual system that contains two short-period giant planets. The TDVs measured for TOI-2535 b represent one of the most extreme examples of planet-planet interactions driving orbital evolution on human timescales.         |

| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.14437-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14437) | **Dwarf galaxy simulations with stellar-core mass- and metallicity-dependent core-collapse supernova explosion energies**  |
|| N. Lahén, <mark>K. Maltsev</mark>, T. Naab, H.-T. Janka |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-12*|
|*Comments*| *20 pages, 14 figures, submitted to MNRAS*|
|**Abstract**|            Core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are a critical source of thermal and kinetic energy and chemically enriched material in galaxies. Leveraging recent advances in CCSN modelling, we implement a novel core-mass- and metallicity-dependent prescription for stellar explodability and CCSN explosion energies, $E_\mathrm{expl}$, in the SPHGal galaxy evolution code. It accounts for black hole (BH) formation via SN failures and via partial fallback of ejecta mass, and adopts an explosion-progenitor connection calibrated to three-dimensional CCSN simulations, such that $E_\mathrm{expl}$ varies between $<0.1$-$2\, \mathrm{B}$. We ran simulations of isolated low-metallicity galaxies with variations in the input stellar feedback models. With the new explodability prescription nearly three times more BHs form compared to the canonical CCSN-model, but the reduced number of successful CCSNe has minimal impact on galactic star formation owing to the low fraction of failed CCSNe. While BH formation contributes to removal of matter from the galactic baryon cycle, the latter remains driven by galactic outflows, and most compact remnant mass is stored in white dwarves. The most significant change is instead brought about by the new average-$E_\mathrm{expl}$ that amounts to $\sim33$\% of the $1\,\mathrm{B}=10^{51}\, \mathrm{erg}$ traditionally assumed in sub-resolution CCSN-models. This reduction results in increased and less bursty star formation, reduced outflows and mass-loading factors, increased star cluster formation efficiency, and enhanced chemical enrichment and metal-recycling in star-forming regions. These results stand in contrast with outflow-launching and baryon cycle modelling in lower-resolution galaxy simulations in which canonical (i.e., $1\, \mathrm{B}$) CCSN feedback is typically assumed to produce galaxy models that match observed scaling relations.         |

| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.13033-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13033) | **Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps**  |
|| B. Zhao, et al. -- incl., <mark>Y. Wang</mark> |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-12*|
|*Comments*| *16 pages, 16 figures, submitted to MNRAS*|
|**Abstract**|            HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.         |

| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.13829-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13829) | **Stable cosmology under flexible covariances: Rescaling and cross-survey correlations in DESI BAO and supernova data**  |
|| E.-A. Kolonia, H. Li, <mark>H. Zhang</mark>, N. Afshordi |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-12*|
|*Comments*| *21 pages, 12 figures, 7 tables*|
|**Abstract**|            Combinations of cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), and Type Ia supernova (SN) data currently favor evolving dark energy over $\Lambda$CDM at the $\sim 3$--$4\sigma$ level, making it important to test whether this preference could be driven by imperfectly modeled uncertainties. We introduce a phenomenological framework in which the published covariance of each dataset is rescaled by a free parameter and the SN compilations are allowed effective cross-survey correlations. We apply it to DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 temperature and polarization data, and a joint likelihood of Pantheon+, Union3, and DES-Dovekie constructed on a common redshift basis. The DESI, Union3, and DES-Dovekie data are consistent with their published covariances, while Pantheon+ shows a mild preference for additional covariance. In all cases the data still allow error bars up to $\sim 1.7$ times larger than published at 95% credibility, yet freeing the rescaling parameters improves the best fit by $\Delta\chi^2 < 1$. Pantheon+ and Union3 exhibit a clear positive effective correlation, $r\simeq 0.4$--$0.5$, plausibly reflecting their shared supernovae; the Pantheon+--DES-Dovekie correlation is weaker and model dependent, and the Union3--DES-Dovekie correlation is consistent with zero. The added covariance freedom broadens the cosmological constraints without shifting them: for the full data combination, the improvement of $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM changes only from $\Delta\chi^2 = 12.8$ to $12.3$ (nominally $3.15\sigma$ to $3.07\sigma$). The preference for evolving dark energy is therefore robust to covariance misestimation of the form considered here.         |

| [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2611.14233-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14233) | **Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory**  |
|| P. A. Collaboration, et al. |
|*Appeared on*| *2026-11-12*|
|*Comments*| *19 pages, 7 figures*|
|**Abstract**|            Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.         |
